args.summary: checkout-api was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1, with an error rate of 18%. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error (partial_failure), leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1; a second rollback attempt completed successfully in all three regions. Post-rollback status: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate 0.2%. Follow-up needed: root-cause v2.3.1 failure (note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging) and investigate the orchestrator error that interrupted the first rollback.

trace.final:
The incident was created despite the timeout (INC-0001), so no retry was needed — avoiding a duplicate page.

**Summary of actions:**

1. **Diagnosed:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy with an 18% error rate. Release history showed v2.3.0 as the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy, so it was not a candidate).
2. **Rolled back to v2.3.0:** The first attempt hit an orchestrator error and halted after us-east, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1. I retried, and the second rollback completed in all three regions.
3. **Verified:** All regions now on v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down to 0.2%.
4. **Opened SEV2 incident INC-0001** for checkout-api describing the failure, the rollback (including the partial failure and retry), the post-rollback state, and follow-ups (root-cause v2.3.1, investigate the orchestrator error).

**Note for follow-up:** v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the cause is understood — it has never been healthy in production, so any redeploy would require change-manager approval under org policy.
